newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Pharma group Ares-Serono has buoyant outlook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Pharma group Ares-Serono has buoyant outlook.

text.p: Ares-Serono, a leader in fertility treatment and the third biggest Swiss pharmaceuticals group, on Wednesday predicted continued sales growth in 1997 in a world of ageing would-be mums having difficulty conceiving.
The group also forecast higher sales in the area of biotechnology as well as immunology drugs and growth hormones for a growing number of menopausal women in the rich world.

At a news conference on 1996 results announced earlier this month, executive director Ernesto Bertarelli said the firm would reinforce its U.S. presence with joint ventures or acquisitions and invest more than $300 million globally in the next three years.
"We see double-digit growth in the next five years," he said.

Ares-Serono's 1996 net profits rose 82 percent on higher sales and margins to $53.5 million. The company last year launched Gonal-F, the first genetically engineered fertility hormone to come to market.
Ares-Serono's biggest business is infertility drugs -- 67 percent of 1996 sales totalling 805 million, up 18 percent. In the past its clients have included actress Sophia Loren
Statistics show one in six couples have difficulty conceiving, one in 10 need professional help and more than a third unable to conceive suffer from unexplained infertility.
Some studies suggest male infertility is also growing because of the stresses of modern life.
Ares-Serono officials said they were also seeking to tap potentially big markets in the developing world where increasing numbers of women were delaying pregnancy in favour of work.
Rubio Sandi, vice-president for Europe, said emerging markets such as South America, the Far East, China, Hong Kong as well as East Europe offered huge potential.

"More and more women in the developing world are working and delaying pregnancy. Women at 32 are not as fertile as they were at the age of 18. That's our business and we believe the market will continue to grow," he said.
Sales of infertility drugs rose 27.5 percent in 1996 to $542.7 million. Nearly half were in Metrodin HP, whose sales jumped 61.2 percent to $254.5 million.

Sales to Europe, the biggest market accounting for half of the total, rose 17.4 percent to $384 million, led by Italy with $117 million, Germany with $60 million, France with $56 million, Spain with $55 million and Britain with $54 million.
Strong sales groth was also recorded in the other regions with Asia Pacific up 46 percent, export operations up 47 percent, Oceania 31 percent and Latin America 14 percent.

Analysts said the company had a bright outlook for 1997 and reported foreign buying in its shares, which jumped to 1,805 francs on Wednesday from a close of 1,755 on Tuesday -- compared to 1,275 at the start of this year.
"Ares-Serono is growing as a top-tier biotechnology stock in the world," said Jean Jacques Sunier, analyst at Switzerland's biggest private bank, Geneva-based Pictet & Cie.
Ares-Serono expects 90 percent or more of its sales to come from genetically-engineered drugs by 2000.

Its second most important product is Serostim, used to treat AIDS-associated weight loss. Its main market is the United States which the company says has an estimated 850,000 HIV positive people and some 200,000 AIDS sufferers.
It is also active in treatment of multiple sclerosis and has launched a recombinant interferon treatment, Rebif, for which it estimates the potential Europe market at more than $1 billion.
